lines: In this replay of an earlier conversation, Aydin Senkut argues venture is an outlier business, so rigid limits on geography, sector focus or ownership targets make firms miss the biggest winners.

He says Felicis wins deals through thesis-driven research and relentless pursuit of likely market leaders, citing early access to Shopify and Canva and willingness to lead rounds in places like Ottawa, Helsinki and Amsterdam.

Diligence, in his view, should hunt for non-obvious insights such as a distribution edge or counter-intuitive product strategy, and a founder's ability to define and measure success (pipeline coverage, revenue retention) signals operating maturity.
Senkut credits his time at Google and Silicon Graphics for his founder-first approach: earning trust through conviction and hands-on help at critical moments regardless of check size.
In a high-valuation market he stresses contingency planning with multiple plan Bs, a lean and diverse team, and cutting non-essential meetings to stay available for portfolio inflection points.
podcast: Capital Allocators – Inside the Institutional Investment Industry
title: [REPLAY] Aydin Senkut – Tenacious Sourcing and Founder Support at Felicis, Venture is Eating the Investment World 6 (EP.234)
